hints: Because the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is uniform throughout both segments $RA$ and $RB$ of the string.
The segment $RA$ makes $45^\circ$ with the vertical. Since $\angle ARB = 90^\circ$, the segment $RB$ also makes $45^\circ$ with the vertical.
Resolve horizontally: both string tensions pull to the right, balanced by the horizontal component of the $2.5\text{ N}$ force: $T\cos 45^\circ + T\cos 45^\circ = 2.5\cos 45^\circ$.
Resolve vertically or along $BR$ to determine the mass $m$ from the weight $mg$.
walkthrough: Because the string is smooth and continuous through ring $R$, the tension $T$ is identical in sections $RA$ and $RB$. Since $AR$ is at $45^\circ$ to the vertical and $\angle ARB = 90^\circ$, line $BR$ is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the vertical.

Resolve forces horizontally to find the tension $T$:
$$T\sin 45^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ = 2.5\sin 45^\circ$$
$$2T\sin 45^\circ = 2.5\sin 45^\circ$$
$$2T = 2.5 \implies T = 1.25\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
The upward vertical component of tension in $RA$ is $T\cos 45^\circ$, while in $RB$ the downward vertical component of tension is $T\cos 45^\circ$. These cancel each other ($T\cos 45^\circ - T\cos 45^\circ = 0$).
The upward vertical component of the $2.5\text{ N}$ force balances the downward weight $mg$:
$$2.5\cos 45^\circ = mg$$
$$mg = 2.5\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 1.25\sqrt{2} \approx 1.7678\text{ N}$$

Solve for the mass $m$ using $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$m = \frac{1.25\sqrt{2}}{10} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{8} \approx 0.1768 \approx 0.177\text{ kg}$$
teacher_walkthrough: State the mechanical property of a smooth ring threaded on a continuous light string: the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the entire string, so $T_{RA} = T_{RB} = T$.

Analyze the geometry of the forces acting at ring $R$:
- $A$ is vertically above $B$.
- Segment $RA$ is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the upward vertical.
- Angle $\angle ARB = 90^\circ$, so segment $RB$ is perpendicular to $RA$ and inclined at $45^\circ$ below the horizontal (or $45^\circ$ to the downward vertical).
- The applied force of $2.5\text{ N}$ acts along the direction $BR$, which is directed upwards and to the left at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking rightwards as positive):
$$\Sigma F_x = 0$$
$$T\sin 45^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ - 2.5\sin 45^\circ = 0$$
$$2T\sin 45^\circ = 2.5\sin 45^\circ$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation (taking upwards as positive):
$$\Sigma F_y = 0$$
$$T\cos 45^\circ - T\cos 45^\circ + 2.5\cos 45^\circ - mg = 0$$
The tensions cancel in the vertical direction:
$$2.5\cos 45^\circ = mg$$

Substitute $\cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2.5 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 10m$$
$$1.25\sqrt{2} = 10m$$
Divide by $10$:
$$m = \frac{1.25\sqrt{2}}{10} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{8} \approx 0.17678 \approx 0.177\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves horizontally to find $T = 1.25\text{ N}$, and resolves vertically to get $mg = 2.5\sin 45^\circ \implies m = 0.177\text{ kg}$.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Resolves tensions and applied force along horizontal and vertical axes.
